reader.requirement: For an external relative file connector, every file control entry in the run unit that describes it must specify the same access mode (an omitted ACCESS MODE clause being sequential), data-name-1 of the RELATIVE KEY phrase must be an external data item, and each entry's RELATIVE KEY phrase must reference that same external data item; a run unit that breaks any part must not be accepted.

reader.notes: All three parts are checked across the describers of one compilation group; the access mode is also in the SelectFingerprint the run time compares across separately compiled elements (not probed: one source holds both programs). An entry that omits the RELATIVE KEY phrase while another names the external item is refused (COBOL1575), a reading of GR1f/GR8 that treats a missing phrase as a different item; it rejects no source the text plainly allows.

refuter.evidence: New accepting probes at --std 85: r5noKey-001 (both entries ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL with no RELATIVE KEY phrase) ran, 'B[FIRST-REC ]'; r5qual-002 (RELATIVE KEY IS REL-KEY against RELATIVE KEY IS REL-KEY OF EXT-KEYS) ran, 'B[FIRST-REC ]'. The doubt: r5offrnd-001: program A describes '01 EXT-KEYS IS EXTERNAL. 05 REL-KEY PIC 9(4). 05 FILLER PIC X(4).', program B describes the same external record as '05 FILLER PIC X(4). 05 REL-KEY PIC 9(4).'; both entries are ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM RELATIVE KEY IS REL-KEY. It compiled with no diagnostic and ran: A wrote records 2 and 3 through positions 1-4, B moved 2 to its REL-KEY and read 'B[SECOND-REC] KEYS[00030002]': the two entries' keys are different storage (positions 1-4 hold 3, positions 5-8 hold 2). The compile-time check (ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check -> SameItem over DataItem.ExternalItemIdentity) compares the name path 'EXT-KEYS.REL-KEY' only, while the same file's RECORD KEY identity (FileEntryIdentity.KeyEntry) includes the byte offset. 1985 lets each program describe an external record's subordinate items its own way as long as the record name and size agree (cite.py 'OK  §1985:X.4.5.4 GR2 ... the text is in GR2' for 'each record-name of the associated record description entries must be the same and the records must define the same number of standard data format characters'), so a same-named item at another position is not obviously 'that same external data item' (cite.py 'OK  §1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR8 ... the text is in GR8'). Two readings decide it: (1) whether 'the same external data item' is the same name path or the same character positions of the external record; (2) whether GR8, a rule on the run unit, obliges the compiler to refuse at all (the reader's requirement says it must not be accepted). Under the reader's own requirement and reading (1) by position, r5offrnd is a run unit that breaks GR8 and is accepted, which would OVERTURN; under the name-path reading, or if GR8 obliges no detection, CONFORMS stands. Class c: the reader's COBOL0900 for a free-standing RELATIVE KEY clause is confirmed by r5omitA-001 at 85.

adjudication.reason: Two programs that describe one external relative file may name RELATIVE KEY items of the same name at DIFFERENT character positions of the external record, and the compiler accepts it: it identifies the item by its name path alone. See below: decided.
